source.title: Geodesic Nets: Some Examples and Open Problems

accepted.question_text: Let M be a closed Riemannian manifold, meaning compact and without boundary. Must M contain a connected closed geodesic multinet, that is, a finite connected immersed multigraph in M whose edges are non-constant geodesic segments between vertices, may intersect or self-intersect, and carry positive integer multiplicities, such that the multiplicity-weighted sum of outgoing unit tangent vectors at every vertex is zero, and such that the multinet contains no non-trivial periodic geodesic?

evidence.quote: Geodesic multinets are defined in the same way with the two following distinctions: 1) Edges are allowed to intersect and self-intersect; 2) Each edge is endowed with a positive integer multiplicity;
Problem 2.0.1. Is it true that each closed Riemannian manifold contains a closed geodesic multinet not containing a non-trivial periodic geodesic?

accepted.question_text: Classify all finite connected 3-regular graphs G for which the standard round 3-sphere S^3 admits a connected embedded closed geodesic net modelled on G; equivalently, determine exactly which such G can be realized by an embedding into S^3 whose edges are distinct non-constant geodesic arcs, with no self-intersections or edge crossings except at common endpoints, and such that at every vertex the sum of the outgoing unit tangent vectors of the three incident edges is zero.

evidence.quote: A geodesic net on M consists of a finite set V of points of M (called vertices) that includes S and a finite set E of non-constant distinct geodesics between vertices (called edges)
Problem 2.0.2. Classify all 3-regular graphs G such that the round 3-sphere has a geodesic net modelled on G.

accepted.question_text: Does every closed Riemannian manifold M of dimension at least 3 admit a connected closed geodesic net modelled on the theta graph, namely a finite embedded geodesic net with empty boundary set whose underlying graph has two vertices joined by three distinct edges and whose balancing condition holds at both vertices?

evidence.quote: The corresponding closed geodesic net consists of two vertices connected by 3 distinct geodesics, so that all angles between each pair of geodesics at each of the vertices are equal to 120◦.
Problem 2.0.3. Is it true that each closed Riemannian manifold of dimension ≥ 3 has a θ-graph shaped closed geodesic net?

accepted.question_text: For a fixed closed Riemannian manifold M, does there exist a function f_M from possible lengths to nonnegative integers, depending only on the geometry and topology of M, such that every finite connected embedded closed geodesic net on M of total length L has at most f_M(L) balanced vertices, where closed means the boundary or unbalanced vertex set is empty and degree-2 balanced vertices are suppressed?

evidence.quote: we are going to consider below only geodesic nets where all balanced vertices have degree ≥ 3.

Problem 2.0.4 (Becker-Kahn). Let M be a closed Riemannian manifold. Is there a function fM (depending on geometry and topology of M) such that each closed geodesic net on M of length L has at most fM(L) (balanced) vertices?

accepted.question_text: Let Sigma be the subset of (R^2)^3 consisting of triples S = (p1, p2, p3) for which, for every integer N, there exists a finite connected geodesic multinet in the Euclidean plane whose unbalanced vertices are exactly p1, p2, p3, whose edges are straight-line segments carrying positive integer multiplicities and may intersect or self-intersect, whose balanced vertices satisfy the multiplicity-weighted zero-sum tangent condition, and whose number of balanced vertices is at least N. Must Sigma have Lebesgue measure zero in (R^2)^3?

evidence.quote: In this case above definition says that a geodesic multinet is a graph G = (V, E) in Rn such that 1) S is a subset of the set of vertices V , 2) each edge is a straight line segment between its endpoints, and is endowed with a positive integer multiplicity

Problem 3.1.3. Let Σ be the set of all triples S of points of the Euclidean plane such that there exist geodesic multinets with 3 unbalanced vertices at S and arbitrarily many balanced vertices. Is it true that Σ is a set of measure zero (in (R2)3)?

accepted.question_text: For each positive integer n, does there exist a function f(n) such that every finite connected geodesic multinet in R^2 with exactly three boundary or unbalanced vertices, no edge joining two unbalanced vertices, all balanced vertices of degree at least 3, and every edge carrying positive integer multiplicity at most n, has at most f(n) balanced vertices?

evidence.quote: Geodesic multinets are defined in the same way with the two following distinctions: 1) Edges are allowed to intersect and self-intersect; 2) Each edge is endowed with a positive integer multiplicity;

Problem 3.1.4. Is there a function f (n) such that for each geodesic multinet with three boundary vertices in the Euclidean plane such the that multiplicities of all edges do not exceed n the number of balanced vertices does not exceed f (n)?

accepted.question_text: Classify all finite connected geodesic multinets in the Euclidean plane with exactly three unbalanced vertices; such a multinet is a finite connected multigraph in R^2 whose edges are straight-line segments with positive integer multiplicities, whose edges may intersect or self-intersect, whose balanced vertices satisfy the multiplicity-weighted zero-sum tangent condition, with degree-2 balanced vertices suppressed and no edge having both endpoints unbalanced.

evidence.quote: Our final convention is that we are going to consider here only connected geodesic (multi)nets
Problem 3.1.5. Classify all geodesic multinets in the Euclidean plane with 3 unbalanced vertices.

accepted.question_text: Construct a finite connected irreducible geodesic net in the Euclidean plane with exactly four unbalanced vertices and more than 16 balanced vertices, or prove that no such net exists. The net must have distinct straight-line edges that meet only at common endpoints, satisfy the zero-sum unit-tangent balancing condition at every balanced vertex, and be irreducible in the sense that no proper subset of its edges, together with all vertices incident to those edges, forms a geodesic net with the same four unbalanced vertices.

evidence.quote: one can define irreducible geodesic nets on a given set S of unbalanced vertices as geodesic nets such that no subgraph formed by a proper subset of the set of edges (with all incident vertices) is a geodesic net with the same set S of unbalanced vertices.
Problem 3.2.1. Find an irreducible geodesic net with 4 unbalanced vertices in the Euclidean plane with more than 16 balanced vertices (or prove that such a geodesic net does not exist.)

accepted.question_text: For every integer B at least 1, does there exist a finite connected embedded geodesic net in the Euclidean plane with exactly four unbalanced vertices and at least B balanced vertices, with straight multiplicity-one edges, no self-intersections or crossings except at common endpoints, no edges between unbalanced vertices, and balanced vertices satisfying the zero-sum unit-tangent condition? Can this already be achieved when the four unbalanced vertices are the vertices of a square?
accepted.context_brief: unbounded balanced vertices from four planar boundary points

evidence.quote: Conjecture 3.2.2. There exist geodesic nets in the Euclidean plane with 4 unbalanced vertices and an arbitrarily large number of balanced vertices. (Moreover, we will not be surprised if this assertion is already true in the case when the set of unbalanced vertices coincides with the set of vertices of a square).

accepted.question_text: Does there exist a universal integer N such that every finite connected irreducible embedded geodesic net in Euclidean 3-space whose unbalanced vertices are exactly the four vertices of a regular tetrahedron has at most N balanced vertices, where edges are straight-line segments, intersections away from common endpoints are disallowed, balanced vertices satisfy the zero-sum unit-tangent condition, and irreducible means no proper edge subgraph is a geodesic net with the same unbalanced vertices?

evidence.quote: when 4 unbalanced vertices are non co-planar points in the Euclidean 3-space, e.g. the vertices of the regular tetrahedron.
Problem 3.2.3. Is there a number N such that each irreducible geodesic net with unbalanced vertices at all vertices of a regular tetrahedron has at most N balanced vertices?

accepted.question_text: Does there exist an integer N0 and a fixed N0-tuple S of points in the Euclidean plane such that, for every integer N at least 1, there is a finite connected embedded geodesic net whose set of unbalanced vertices is exactly S and whose number of balanced vertices is greater than N? Moreover, does the collection of such N0-tuples contain a subset of (R^2)^N0 of positive Lebesgue measure, or even a nonempty open subset?
accepted.context_brief: fixed boundary tuple with unbounded planar nets

evidence.quote: Conjecture 3.3.1. 1. There exist N0 and an N0 -tuple S such that for each N there exists a geodesic net with S being its set of unbalanced vertices and the number of balanced vertices greater than N . 2. Furthermore, there exist not merely one such N0 -tuple S but a subset of (R2 )N0 of positive measure (or even a non-empty open subset) of such N0 -tuples.

accepted.question_text: Does there exist a bound for the number of balanced vertices of any finite connected embedded geodesic net in the Euclidean plane that depends only on the number of unbalanced vertices and the total imbalance, where the imbalance vector at an unbalanced vertex is the sum of all outgoing unit tangent vectors along incident edges and the total imbalance is the sum of the norms of these imbalance vectors over all unbalanced vertices?

evidence.quote: We call this sum the imbalance vector Imb(v) at v, and its norm the imbalance, imb(v), at v. The sum of imbalances v∈S imb(v) over the set of all unbalanced points is called the total imbalance of the geodesic net.
Conjecture 3.4.1 (M. Gromov). The number of balanced vertices of a geodesic net in the Euclidean plane can be bounded above in terms of the number of unbalanced vertices and the total imbalance.

accepted.question_text: Does there exist a function f such that every finite connected geodesic multinet in the Euclidean plane, with straight-line edges carrying positive integer multiplicities, allowing edge intersections and self-intersections, satisfying the multiplicity-weighted balancing condition at each balanced vertex, and having n unbalanced vertices, diameter D, and total length L counted with multiplicity, has fewer than f(L/D, n) balanced vertices?

evidence.quote: Conjecture 3.4.2. There exists a function f of such that each geodesic multinet in the Euclidean plane with n unbalanced vertices, diameter D, and total length L has less than f (L/D, n) balanced vertices.

accepted.question_text: Let M be a complete Riemannian manifold. Does there exist a function f_M, depending on M but invariant under rescaling of the metric, such that every finite connected geodesic net G on M with n unbalanced vertices, total length L, diameter D, and adjusted total length L_tilde has at most f_M(L_tilde, L/D, n) balanced vertices? Here L_tilde is the sum over all arclength-parametrized edges e(s) of the integral of 1/inj_M(e(s)) ds, where inj_M(x) is the injectivity radius at x. In particular, if M has positive injectivity radius inj(M), must every such G have at most f_M(L/inj(M), L/D, n) balanced vertices?

evidence.quote: The adjusted total length L̃ of a geodesic net is the sum of integrals over all edges ei parametrized by their respective arclengths of 1 / inj(ei(s)), where inj(ei(s)) denotes the injectivity radius of the ambient Riemannian manifold at ei(s).

Conjecture 3.4.3 (Boundedness conjecture for geodesic nets on Riemannian manifolds). Let M be a complete Riemannian manifold. There exists a function fM which depends on M but is invariant with respect to rescalings of M with the following property: Let G be a geodesic net on M with total length L, adjusted length L̃ and diameter D that has n unbalanced vertices. Then its number of balanced vertices does not exceed fM (L̃, L / D, n). In particular, if M has injectivity radius inj > 0, then the number of balanced vertices does not exceed fM (L / inj, L / D, n).

accepted.question_text: Consider the sevenfold star construction of finite geodesic nets G_n(phi). The construction starts from seven equally spaced outer vertices, defines an inner layer V_0 using the fixed algebraic angle alpha_0 = 88/21 radians and a small deviation angle phi, and then recursively builds layers V_i by winging vertices and, when needed, suspending an odd layer from one nearest outer hook or an even layer from two nearest outer hooks. For each layer V_i define a suspension-angle function phi_i(phi): for odd i, phi_i is the angle OPv between the outer-circle center O, the hook P, and the suspended vertex v; for even i, phi_i is the angle OXv, where X is the third vertex of the equilateral triangle on the two hooks P,Q and v is the suspended vertex, with phi_0(phi)=phi. Since every phi_i(0)=0 and the construction depends smoothly on phi, is the derivative sequence phi_i_prime(0) pairwise nonrepeating?

evidence.quote: The construction of the geodesic net Gn (ϕ) relies on two parameters ϕ and n.
Then we define the suspension angle ϕi to be the angle ∠OP v.
Then we define the suspension angle ϕi to be the angle ∠OXv.
Conjecture 4.5.7. ϕ0i (0) is a sequence that never repeats itself.

accepted.question_text: In the finite sevenfold star construction G_n(phi), with layers V_0 through V_n and suspension-angle functions phi_0(phi), phi_1(phi), ..., phi_n(phi) defined from the one-hook and two-hook suspension geometry, is it true that for sufficiently small nonzero phi the finite sequence phi_0(phi), phi_1(phi), ..., phi_n(phi) has no repeated value? If so, does the non-overlap criterion imply that G_n(phi) is a geodesic net rather than merely a geodesic multinet, with every edge having weight one, exactly 14 unbalanced vertices, and arbitrarily many balanced vertices as n is chosen large?

evidence.quote: Lemma 4.5.5. If for any fixed ϕ ∈ (−ϵ, ϵ), the sequence ϕi(ϕ) never repeats itself, all edges of the resulting geodesic net Gn(ϕ) intersect transversally (if at all). In other words, there are no edges with weight other than one.

Conjecture 4.5.8. For small nonzero ϕ ∈ (−ϵ, ϵ), the sequence ϕi (ϕ) never repeats itself. This implies that Gn (ϕ) is a geodesic net for which all edges have weight one. So this Gn (ϕ) would in fact fulfill all required conditions: (a) There are 14 unbalanced vertices. (b) For n large enough, we can achieve an arbitrarily large number of balanced vertices. (c) All edges have weight one.

accepted.question_text: Let a geodesic net with exactly three unbalanced vertices A1, A2, A3 be drawn on a Riemannian plane, with geodesic edges and balanced vertices satisfying the zero-sum unit-tangent condition. Parsch proved that on any nonpositively curved Riemannian plane such a net has exactly one balanced vertex O at the Fermat point of A1, A2, A3 and exactly the three edges OA1, OA2, and OA3. Does the same rigidity conclusion remain true under the weaker assumption that the integral of the positive part of the curvature is sufficiently small?

evidence.quote: Theorem 3.1.2 ([Par18]). A geodesic net with 3 unbalanced vertices A1 , A2 , A3 in the Euclidean plane has exactly one balanced vertex O at the Fermat point of the three unbalanced vertices and three edges OAi . Moreover, this assertion is true for geodesic nets with 3 unbalanced vertices on any non-positively curved Riemannian R2 .

Yet it is not known if the assertion is still true if the integral of the positive part of the curvature is sufficiently small. (The example for positive curvature constructed in [Par18] requires total curvature at least π.)
